court: In the High Court of Madras
advocates: For Respondent: Mr. U. Baranidharan, Special Government Pleader
judgment_text:
Petition filed under Article 226 of The Constitution of India praying for the issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the respondent to register the sale deed under TP/243083554/2025 in favour of the petitioner.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

Senthilkumar Ramamoorthy, J.:— Intending to purchase a property, the petitioner paid sale consideration to the vendor and presented the executed sale deed for registration on 22.12.2025. According to the petitioner, he was orally informed that the property should be valued in square foot because the adjacent properties have been so valued. The present writ petition has been filed in the said facts and circumstances.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner invited my attention to the sale deed and patta to emphasise that the property is classified as Nanjai land. He also points out that the sale consideration is higher than the guideline value.

3. Mr. U. Baranidharan, learned Special Government Pleader, accepts notice for the sole respondent. He submits that the petitioner may be directed to re-present the document and that the registering officer would either register the same or issue a speaking order of refusal.

4. Considering the above submissions, this writ petition is disposed of on the following terms:

4.1 The petitioner shall re-present the sale deed within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order;

4.2 Within two weeks from such representation, subject to fulfillment of other requirements relating to registration, the registering officer shall either register the document or issue a speaking order of refusal, after providing a reasonable opportunity to the petitioner.

There shall be no order as to costs.
